policy_title: Deliver Family Hub in Every Local Authority
stated: The Conservative Party will go further to deliver a Family Hub in every local authority in England, supporting families from early years through to adulthood with a range of services.

source.quote: Our plan has already delivered Family Hubs in over 75 local authorities. We will go further to deliver a Family Hub in every local authority in England.

bearing_set.reason: Family Hubs are explicitly built around early-years support and parenting services; early intervention is directly linked to school readiness, the attainment gap, and children's developmental outcomes — a real verdict on education & opportunity.

Family Hubs typically integrate health visiting, perinatal mental health, and infant/child health services; expanding their reach would plausibly affect healthcare access for families, earning a real verdict on healthcare.

Family Hubs are by design community-gathering institutions intended to reduce isolation, build inter-family and inter-agency trust, and foster local social connections — directly bearing on social trust and belonging indicators.

Providing publicly-funded family support services (parenting advice, early-language help, mental health access) that better-off families currently purchase privately has a plausible equalising mechanism — if consistently deployed in deprived areas it narrows outcome gaps between income groups.

membership_note: A multi-service community institution touches education/opportunity (O7) most strongly, with genuine secondary bearings on health access (O3), social cohesion (O15), and inequality (O14) via the substitution of public provision for what higher-income families purchase privately. Fiscal effect is real but modest relative to total public spending and left out of O12 absent a specified cost or funding gap.
